questions.prompt: What are we told about the cost of casting and tuning a bell?

options.text: Tuning is billed by the hour and always takes a larger share of the price than the metal.
Founders quote a single price for each kilo that covers the casting and the tuning together.
Time on the lathe rises with a bell's weight, so a bell of a tonne takes far longer to tune.
Tuning can cost more than the bronze on a small bell, and less than it on a heavy one.

questions.prompt: What does the text say about the way Vivienne Corvenden tunes a bell?

options.text: She tunes every partial to a closer tolerance than Kerrig does and records the figure for each.
She brings three of the partials into close tune and leaves the minor third roughly as cast.
She works from the mould instead, controlling wall thickness so that little lathe work is needed.
She settles the minor third first and lets the hum fall wherever the casting happens to leave it.

questions.prompt: What is implied about a founder who intends to tune all five partials tightly?

options.text: The bell has to leave the mould heavier, since the metal tuning removes must be there first.
Thinning the wall at any one height pulls every partial in the bell down with it.
The bell will need heavier fittings and a stronger frame to carry the extra work.
Any bell tuned that closely will always sound thinner than one left as it came from the mould.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's attitude towards the disagreement between Voregg and Corvenden?

options.text: Mildly persuaded by Corvenden, he treats the trial at Ockthorne as the nearest thing to proof.
He treats the disagreement as a matter of taste that measurement can never settle.
He sets out both positions and the single trial that bears on them without picking a side.
He regards Corvenden's objection as workshop folklore that the measurements have already disposed of.

questions.prompt: What is this text mainly about?

options.text: How the hours a bell spends on the tuning lathe largely decide the price a parish pays.
